title: uField Broker Comparison
prompt: For inter-vehicle messaging, compare uFldNodeBroker, uFldShoreBroker, uFldNodeComms, and uFldMessageHandler. What does each one do, and what is a common symptom when each is misconfigured?

Think of the path as:

vehicle announces itself → shore learns how to reach it → shore routes/simulates node-to-node messages → receiving vehicle unpacks the message into a local MOOS variable.

Tool	Usually runs where	Main job	Common misconfiguration symptom
uFldNodeBroker	Vehicle community	Tells shoreside, “I am vehicle X; reach my pShare at this host/IP/port/community.” It sends the vehicle’s local connection info to the shore broker. 
Ocean AI
+1
	Shore never really “knows” the vehicle. You may see NODE_REPORTs locally, but shoreside does not establish the expected bridge back to that vehicle. Messages to the vehicle never arrive because shore has wrong/missing host, pShare port, or community name.
uFldShoreBroker	Shoreside community	Receives vehicle broker info and asks shoreside pShare to create bridges to each known vehicle. It can create per-vehicle bridge variables such as FOO_ALL / FOO_JAKE style routes depending on config. 
Ocean AI
+1
	Vehicles may announce themselves, but bridges are not created correctly. Symptom: shore sees some registration/broker traffic, but variables meant to go back out to vehicles do not cross. Often caused by wrong bridge variable list, wrong pShare setup, or inconsistent vehicle/community names.
uFldNodeComms	Shoreside community	Manages inter-vehicle communication logic. It uses incoming node reports/positions and can impose range limits, message size/frequency limits, or team-based blocking. It forwards valid NODE_MESSAGE traffic toward the destination vehicle. 
Ocean AI
+1
	Vehicles are visible on shore, but messages are selectively missing. A message may be dropped because the destination name is wrong, the vehicles are “out of comms range,” rate/size limits are exceeded, teams do not match, or NODE_REPORTs are stale/missing.
uFldMessageHandler	Receiving vehicle community	Unpacks an incoming node message and posts the embedded variable/value pair into the local MOOSDB. For example, a message payload can become a normal local variable that behaviors or apps can subscribe to. 
Ocean AI
+1
	The vehicle receives an incoming message variable, but the expected local payload variable never appears. Symptom: you might see NODE_MESSAGE / incoming comms traffic in uXMS, but not the final variable like SWIMMER_ALERT, TASK_ASSIGNMENT, etc. Often caused by not running uFldMessageHandler, wrong subscription/input variable, malformed message string, or mismatched destination/source fields.

A useful debugging mental model:

No vehicle registration at shore → suspect uFldNodeBroker, pHostInfo, vehicle name, host/IP, pShare UDP port, or launch arguments.

Registration exists but no pShare bridge back → suspect uFldShoreBroker or shoreside pShare bridge configuration.

Bridge exists, vehicles visible, but messages are blocked/dropped → suspect uFldNodeComms rules: destination, range, stale reports, team, size, or rate.

Incoming message reaches the vehicle but the useful variable is absent → suspect uFldMessageHandler or message formatting.

The most common trap is mixing up transport/configuration with payload delivery. uFldNodeBroker and uFldShoreBroker help establish how communities can talk through pShare; uFldNodeComms decides whether a node-to-node message should be passed; uFldMessageHandler turns the received message into the actual local MOOS variable your app or behavior cares about.

claude.text:
These four modules are all part of the MOOS-IvP multi-vehicle framework, sitting in the uFld suite.

These four modules are all part of the MOOS-IvP multi-vehicle framework, sitting in the uFld suite. Here's how they divide up the problem:

uFldNodeBroker

What it does: Runs on each vehicle and registers the vehicle with the shoreside community. It sends periodic "node reports" up to the shore, and negotiates which MOOS variables get bridged from the vehicle to shore (and vice versa). Think of it as the vehicle's ambassador to the shore.

Common misconfiguration symptom: The vehicle never appears in the shoreside community. If BRIDGE lines are wrong or the HOST/PORT of the shoreside isn't correctly specified, the vehicle stays isolated — no node reports reach shore, and no shoreside commands reach the vehicle.

uFldShoreBroker

What it does: Runs on the shore and is the counterpart to uFldNodeBroker. It listens for incoming node registrations from vehicles and dynamically creates MOOSDB bridges to each one. It manages the variable routing between the shore community and each vehicle community. Without it, the shore has no idea vehicles exist.

Common misconfiguration symptom: Vehicles connect but nothing flows bidirectionally. A telltale sign is that APPCAST or mission-critical variables (like DEPLOY, RETURN) never make it down to the vehicle — because the QBRIDGE or BRIDGE variable lists on the shore side are incomplete or misnamed.

uFldNodeComms

What it does: Simulates the communication channel between vehicles themselves (not vehicle-to-shore). It runs on the shore and acts as a message relay: vehicles post a message, it goes up to shore via the broker infrastructure, uFldNodeComms decides whether to deliver it to the target vehicle based on a configurable comms model (range limits, drop rates, noise). This is what makes inter-vehicle range-limited communication realistic in simulation.

Common misconfiguration symptom: All vehicles can always talk to each other regardless of distance — i.e., the range model isn't applied. This usually means COMMS_RANGE was never set (so it defaults to unlimited), or the module isn't running at all and messages are just passing through the broker unrestricted.

uFldMessageHandler

What it does: Runs on each vehicle and processes incoming inter-vehicle messages that were delivered by uFldNodeComms. It takes the encoded message payload posted to NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL and republishes the content as a proper MOOS variable in the vehicle's local community, so behaviors can actually react to it. It's the last mile on the receiving end.

Common misconfiguration symptom: Messages arrive at the vehicle (you can see NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL being posted in the MOOSDB) but nothing acts on them. Behaviors that depend on communicated info never update. The fix is usually that uFldMessageHandler isn't in the vehicle's .moos file at all, or the variable name it's configured to republish doesn't match what the behavior is subscribing to.

The Big Picture
VEHICLE A                   SHORE                    VEHICLE B
─────────────────────       ──────────────────────   ─────────────────────
uFldNodeBroker  ──────────► uFldShoreBroker          uFldNodeBroker
                             uFldNodeComms  ─────────►
uFldMessageHandler ◄──────────────────────────────── (delivers to B)

The broker pair handles vehicle ↔ shore routing; uFldNodeComms handles vehicle ↔ vehicle relay with a physics-based comms model; and uFldMessageHandler handles decoding and republishing on the receiving vehicle. Each one being absent or misconfigured produces a distinct failure mode, which is what makes debugging multi-vehicle MOOS-IvP missions a layered process.

gemini.text:
In the MOOS-IvP autonomy ecosystem, inter-vehicle and vehicle-to-shoreside communication relies on a standard pipeline. Understanding the distinction between these applications comes down to separating network connectivity (brokering) from information routing/filtering (messaging).

Here is a breakdown of what each application does and the common symptoms you will observe when they are misconfigured.

1. Connection Discovery & Bridging (The Brokers)

uFldNodeBroker and uFldShoreBroker work together as a pair to automatically configure network connections (pShare) between vehicles and the shoreside station without forcing you to hardcode IP addresses.

uFldNodeBroker (Runs on the Vehicle / Node)

What it does: It gathers local network info (from pHostInfo) and periodically sends initialization "pings" (NODE_BROKER_PING) to potential shoreside IP addresses. Once it receives an acknowledgment, it automatically requests pShare to bridge specific vehicle variables (like NODE_REPORT_LOCAL) over to the shoreside.

Common Misconfiguration Symptom: The vehicle completely vanishes from the shoreside display (pMarineViewer). If you misconfigure the SHORE_IP or port hints in this app's configuration block, the vehicle will ping the wrong location, a network bridge will never be requested, and the shoreside will remain completely blind to the vehicle's existence.

uFldShoreBroker (Runs on the Shoreside / Topside)

What it does: It listens for incoming pings from vehicles. When it hears a valid ping, it records the vehicle's IP/port and tells the shoreside's pShare exactly how to send command-and-control variables (like DEPLOY or RETURN) back out to that specific vehicle.  
MIT Marine Autonomy Lab

Common Misconfiguration Symptom: You can see the vehicle moving on the shoreside map, but it ignores all of your commands. If the bridge macro lines in uFldShoreBroker are mistyped (e.g., mismatching the variable name or omitting a vehicle name macro like $V), the shoreside successfully hears the vehicle, but it fails to build the reverse bridge to send outgoing commands back to the node.

2. Information Routing & Simulation (The Messagers)

uFldNodeComms and uFldMessageHandler handle the actual processing and delivery of simulated inter-vehicle text messages (wrapped as NODE_MESSAGE structures).

uFldNodeComms (Runs on the Shoreside)

What it does: It acts as the "cellular tower" or routing switchboard for the fleet. It tracks where all vehicles are by looking at their NODE_REPORTs. When a vehicle posts an outgoing message, uFldNodeComms intercepts it and determines if it should be delivered based on simulated environment conditions—such as whether the vehicles are within a maximum transmission range (comms_range) or if they are spamming too fast (min_msg_interval).

Common Misconfiguration Symptom: Messages are perfectly transmitted when vehicles are close together, but suddenly stop delivering later, OR they never deliver at all. If you accidentally set comms_range too small (or leave it at a strict default), vehicles will silently drop messages as soon as they drift a few meters apart. Additionally, if uFldNodeComms is missing from the shoreside Antler block entirely, inter-vehicle messages will reach the shore but sit there dead in the water.

uFldMessageHandler (Runs on the Vehicle / Node)

What it does: It acts as the vehicle's mailbox receiver. When a routed NODE_MESSAGE successfully arrives from the shoreside at a vehicle's local MOOSDB, uFldMessageHandler unpacks the payload string (which looks like src=alpha,var=SPEED,val=2.5) and physically posts SPEED = 2.5 to the local MOOSDB so the autonomy system can use it.

Common Misconfiguration Symptom: The NODE_MESSAGE variable updates in the vehicle's DB, but the actual target variable never changes. If you scope the vehicle's database, you will literally see the raw, wrapped message string arrive, but the vehicle doesn't react to it. This means uFldMessageHandler isn't running, isn't subscribed to the right incoming variable, or the message formatting itself is corrupted.

Summary Cheat Sheet
App Name	Where it Runs	Primary Job	Misconfiguration Red Flag
uFldNodeBroker	Vehicle	Initiates network connection to shore.	Vehicle is a "ghost" (never appears on shoreside).
uFldShoreBroker	Shoreside	Approves connections & bridges outward commands.	See the vehicle, but can't control it.
uFldNodeComms	Shoreside	Evaluates range/bandwidth limits & routes messages.	Messages stop delivering when vehicles separate.
uFldMessageHandler	Vehicle	Unpacks incoming messages into native MOOS variables.	Raw message string arrives, but vehicle ignores contents.

chatgpt_55_instant.text:
uFldNodeBroker: runs on each vehicle. It handles the vehicle-side connection into the field messaging system, usually registering the vehicle with shoreside and enabling outgoing/incoming node messages.

Misconfig symptom: vehicle appears alive locally, but shoreside does not know how to route messages to or from it.

uFldShoreBroker: runs on shoreside. It is the central broker/registry for routing messages between vehicles and shoreside.

Misconfig symptom: all vehicle-to-vehicle messaging seems broken, or only local variables update; messages never reach other communities.

uFldNodeComms: often used on the vehicle side to package/transmit node reports and comms-related information through the field comms path.

Misconfig symptom: NODE_REPORT/contact information is stale or missing, so pMarineViewer or other vehicles do not see the vehicle correctly.

uFldMessageHandler: receives NODE_MESSAGE / NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL-style messages and posts the payload variable into the local MOOSDB.

Misconfig symptom: you can see that a message arrived, but the intended payload variable is never posted locally; behaviors/apps waiting on that variable never trigger.

The usual mental model:

vehicle app posts message
        ↓
uFldNodeBroker / comms path
        ↓
uFldShoreBroker
        ↓
destination vehicle broker/comms
        ↓
uFldMessageHandler posts payload variable locally
        ↓
local app or behavior reacts

A good debug test is: first verify NODE_REPORTs and vehicle names, then verify broker registration, then inspect raw NODE_MESSAGE traffic, and finally check whether uFldMessageHandler turns the message into the expected local MOOS variable.

chatgpt_55_low_cli.text:
For inter-vehicle messaging, these apps sit at different layers:

| App | Typical role | Common misconfiguration symptom |
|---|---|---|
| `uFldNodeBroker` | Runs in a vehicle community. Establishes the vehicle’s connection to the shoreside infrastructure, usually by coordinating sharing routes with `pShare`/broker config. It lets the vehicle publish things like `NODE_REPORT` and receive shoreside-routed traffic. | The vehicle does not appear on the shoreside display, or messages never leave/return to the vehicle because the node is not properly connected to shore. |
| `uFldShoreBroker` | Runs shoreside. Counterpart to `uFldNodeBroker`; accepts/coordinates broker connections from vehicles and helps maintain routing between shore and each node. | Vehicles may run normally locally but are not registered/connected at shore, or shore cannot route traffic back to them. |
| `uFldNodeComms` | Handles simulated inter-node message routing. It consumes outgoing node messages, considers destination/range/comms rules, and forwards valid messages toward the destination node. | `NODE_MESSAGE_LOCAL` is posted, but the destination vehicle never receives anything; often caused by wrong node names, missing node reports, range/comms settings, or routing config. |
| `uFldMessageHandler` | Runs on the receiving vehicle. Converts incoming `NODE_MESSAGE` mail into the actual MOOS variable/value requested by the message, e.g. posting `FOO=bar` locally. | The vehicle receives `NODE_MESSAGE`, but the intended local variable is never posted, so the behavior watching that variable never triggers. |

In short: `NodeBroker`/`ShoreBroker` provide the vehicle-shore connectivity, `NodeComms` routes messages between nodes, and `MessageHandler` delivers the received message into the local MOOSDB as the target variable.
